doc.title: Phil Mead interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006

title: Hamilton's music department: Baldwin and Berrian Shute
summary: John Baldwin the choir director and organist, and Professor Shute's record evenings at his home.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Yeah. Well when you were here was there an active music department?

Very much so. John Baldwin had come I think a few years before and of course was starting his reign as just an outstanding choir director, a technically just stupendous organist. I don’t know if you ever were fortunate to hear John play the organ but he really was a wonderful musician. And so there was that, and then there was the jazz which I’m sure we’ll get into. And then Berrian Shute was the old professor of music and used to have us down to his home and we’d listen on the old scratchy 78 records in the evening, we’d listen to opera. It was a different era but it was very intimate and for music that’s the best.
